key_findings.detail: Spark saw sable on about 47% of samples, but only about 1.9% as the code doing the work at that moment.
limitations: It may be on the path without being the heavy part.
Don’t treat this as proof this mod alone made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Lots of XP, dropped items, or glue entities
key_findings.detail: Of 2244 loaded entities: about 53% XP+items, 20% glue-style entities (e.g. Create glue), 72% XP+items+glue combined; top custom is super_glue (~17%).
limitations: These are counts of what is loaded — not proof they made the server lag.
Worth checking in-world first — common lag suspects, not a proven tick cost.

key_findings.title: Most entities are packed into a few chunks
key_findings.detail: The top 20 busy chunks hold 46% of loaded entities (across 537 chunks that have any).
limitations: This helps you know where to look — it does not prove those chunks made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Crowded chunk found
key_findings.detail: overworld chunk -102,-17 has 180 entities (mostly minecraft:experience_orb).
limitations: A crowded chunk is a clue to check in-world — not proof it made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Busy chunks were far from online players
key_findings.detail: 5 busy chunks were at least 28 chunks away from the nearest player in that world (farthest 6785).
limitations: This can mean chunk loaders or leftover loaded areas — the profile cannot prove which.
The profile has no chunk-ticket list, so force-loading is not proven.

key_findings.title: create used a large share of server time
key_findings.detail: About 12.8% of measured Server-thread time was spent inside create itself (hot step: ContinuousOBBCollider.collideMany).
limitations: This shows where time showed up in the sample — not proof this mod alone made the server lag.
Sampling can miss short bursts or mis-label some code.

key_findings.title: Players online during the capture
key_findings.detail: 6 players were online when these stats were collected.
limitations: Player count alone does not say where they were or what they were doing.

key_findings.title: Lag only showed up in part of the capture
key_findings.detail: 1 of 1 one-minute slices missed the target tick speed.
limitations: One-minute slices can hide shorter spikes inside that minute.

key_findings.title: A big chunk of time couldn’t be tied to a clear mod
key_findings.detail: About 31.3% of measured time was labeled unknown or native (JVM/native code or missing mod mapping).
limitations: Unknown/native can mean JVM code, physics natives, or missing class→mod mapping.
Don’t invent a mod name from a package prefix.

key_findings.title: Lag with only moderate CPU use
key_findings.detail: Process CPU was about 25% while ticks looked bad. Minecraft’s tick mostly runs on one thread, so low total CPU does not mean that thread had spare room.
limitations: Moderate total CPU does not mean the tick thread was free.
This pattern does not name which mod or farm is responsible.

key_findings.title: The host machine was using a lot of swap
key_findings.detail: Swap used 44.66 GiB of 98.81 GiB. If the host is actively swapping to disk, the whole machine can hitch for hundreds of ms.
limitations: Other programs on the host can own that swap too.
One snapshot cannot prove swap was thrashing during the worst tick.

key_findings.title: Garbage collection was active
key_findings.detail: About 1850 GC collections were reported in the capture metadata.
limitations: Collection count is not pause length — check average pause time if lag feels hitchy.

key_findings.title: View or simulation distance is set high
key_findings.detail: These settings can add load. Try lowering one of them for a test — not a proven cause by itself.
limitations: Distance alone does not prove chunk loading was the lag.

key_findings.title: AFK players are never kicked for idle
key_findings.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 lets AFK players keep areas loaded forever.
limitations: That’s an ops choice — farm fail-safes matter more than the timeout alone.

key_findings.title: Full entity tracking range with high view distance
key_findings.detail: entity-broadcast-range-percentage=100 with view-distance=20 can make dense entity areas cost more to track for players.
limitations: Tracking cost is a secondary clue — not primary proof of tick lag.

key_findings.title: Neighbor-update chain limit is very high
key_findings.detail: max-chained-neighbor-updates=1000000 can let cascading redstone or machines hitch for longer.
limitations: This is a spike-risk setting — not proof of the worst tick in this capture.

key_findings.title: Spectators can generate new chunks
key_findings.detail: spectatorsGenerateChunks is on — flying in spectator can generate terrain and add load.
limitations: This is an occasional spike risk — not enough alone to explain long low TPS.

recommendations.title: Inspect Overworld chunk -102, -17 first
recommendations.detail: overworld chunk -102,-17 has 180 entities (mostly minecraft:experience_orb). Visit that spot in-game before changing global limits.
actions: Go near blocks ~-1632, ~-272 in Overworld
Note what is producing the XP orbs (farm, hopper line, machine, leftover pile)
Fix or pause that one setup, then profile again with a similar player count
limitations: Clearing entities without fixing what makes them will not prove a lasting fix.
reversible_actions: Go near blocks ~-1632, ~-272 in Overworld
Note what is producing the XP orbs (farm, hopper line, machine, leftover pile)
Fix or pause that one setup, then profile again with a similar player count
recommendations.why: This capture’s busiest chunk is a concrete place to look — clearer than guessing from mod percentages alone.

recommendations.title: Check Create farms and item piles before tweaking Create configs
recommendations.detail: Create shows up in stacks (~12.8% own, ~54% involvement) and the world is heavy on XP/items/glue. Start with the busy chunks and the machines feeding them — a Create config tweak won’t clear a flooded farm.
actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
limitations: A smaller percentage after a change does not prove what fixed the lag.
reversible_actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
recommendations.why: Create time plus a crowded automation/item composition usually means an in-world setup, not a random version bump.

recommendations.title: Check free RAM and whether the machine is swapping
recommendations.detail: Host swap was about 44.7 GiB during this capture. Confirm free memory and active swap before raising Minecraft’s max heap.
actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
limitations: Don’t assume Minecraft alone filled the host’s swap.
reversible_actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
recommendations.why: Swap pressure can hitch the whole machine even when Spark points at mods or entities.

recommendations.title: Lower view-distance from 20 for a short test
recommendations.detail: This capture used view-distance=20 while ticks looked slow. Try 18 temporarily — that cuts how far chunks stay loaded for players without touching simulation yet.
actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
limitations: If the two captures had different player activity, the comparison can be misleading.
reversible_actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
recommendations.why: View distance is high in the captured server.properties, so the advice names that setting instead of a generic tweak.

evidence_summary.what_happened: Your server was lagging — start with the findings below
evidence_summary.why_watchtower_says_this: About 10.1 TPS (about half speed); typical tick ~94 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~121 ms; worst tick ~181 ms (1 min); worst recent hitch ~1.8 s (5 min).
evidence_summary.what_this_cannot_prove: A profile shows what was busy during the capture. It doesn’t prove the single cause or how much faster the server will get.

settings_advice.title: View distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 121ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Memory pressure (heap 43%, RAM 87%) — lower view-distance. Swap 45% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested view-distance=4 (band 6–10).

settings_advice.title: Network compression
settings_advice.detail: Compression threshold 256 is in a common range.

settings_advice.title: Spawn protection
settings_advice.detail: Spawn protection 16 is an ops choice — not a primary lag lever.

settings_advice.title: Simulation distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 121ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Memory pressure (heap 43%, RAM 87%) — lower view-distance. Swap 45% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested simulation-distance=3 (band 4–8). Keep sim ≤ view.

settings_advice.title: Entity broadcast range
settings_advice.detail: With high view-distance/CPU pressure, consider lowering entity broadcast toward 50%.

settings_advice.title: Rate limit
settings_advice.detail: Packet rate-limit 0 — leave alone unless you are mitigating connection abuse.

settings_advice.title: Max tick time
settings_advice.detail: Watchdog headroom looks fine for modded dedicated servers.

settings_advice.title: Player idle timeout
settings_advice.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 never kicks AFK players — they can keep chunks loaded. Consider 30–60 minutes.

settings_advice.title: Sync chunk writes
settings_advice.detail: sync-chunk-writes=true can stutter the tick loop on dedicated hosts — consider false (Paper already forces this).

settings_advice.title: Max chained neighbor updates
settings_advice.detail: Neighbor-update chain limit 1000000 is very high — consider 100000 to limit redstone/hopper storms.

settings_advice.title: Region file compression
settings_advice.detail: deflate is the common default; lz4 is fine on modern JVMs.

settings_advice.title: Native transport
settings_advice.detail: Native transport enabled — fine on Linux.

verdict.headline: Your server was lagging — start with the findings below
verdict.summary: TPS 19.3 · typical tick 51 ms · slow ticks (p95) 62 ms · worst hitch 5.0 s · 4 players · 3848 entities

key_findings.title: CPU time profile
key_findings.detail: Percentages show how often Spark saw each piece of code on the main Server thread during the capture — not every millisecond of the whole machine.
limitations: A profile only covers the time window that was recorded.

key_findings.title: Your server was running slow
key_findings.detail: About 19.3 TPS; typical tick ~51 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~62 ms; worst tick ~386 ms (1 min); worst recent hitch ~5.0 s (5 min).
limitations: These numbers describe the capture window. They do not name a single cause.

key_findings.title: neruina shows up often in the stack, but rarely as the heavy step
key_findings.detail: Spark saw neruina on about 48% of samples, but only about 0.0% as the code doing the work at that moment.
limitations: It may be on the path without being the heavy part.
Don’t treat this as proof this mod alone made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Lots of XP, dropped items, or glue entities
key_findings.detail: Of 3848 loaded entities: about 74% XP+items, 3% glue-style entities (e.g. Create glue), 78% XP+items+glue combined; top custom is honey_glue (~3%).
limitations: These are counts of what is loaded — not proof they made the server lag.
Worth checking in-world first — common lag suspects, not a proven tick cost.

key_findings.title: Most entities are packed into a few chunks
key_findings.detail: The top 20 busy chunks hold 44% of loaded entities (across 665 chunks that have any).
limitations: This helps you know where to look — it does not prove those chunks made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Crowded chunk found
key_findings.detail: the_nether chunk 170,-88 has 455 entities (mostly minecraft:experience_orb).
limitations: A crowded chunk is a clue to check in-world — not proof it made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Busy chunks with nobody in that world
key_findings.detail: 2 busy chunks were in worlds with no located players (the_nether).
limitations: No one online there can mean chunk loaders or leftover loaded farms — not proven from this profile alone.
The profile has no chunk-ticket list, so force-loading is not proven.

key_findings.title: create used a large share of server time
key_findings.detail: About 17.0% of measured Server-thread time was spent inside create itself (hot step: ContinuousOBBCollider.collideMany).
limitations: This shows where time showed up in the sample — not proof this mod alone made the server lag.
Sampling can miss short bursts or mis-label some code.

key_findings.title: Players online during the capture
key_findings.detail: 4 players were online when these stats were collected.
limitations: Player count alone does not say where they were or what they were doing.

key_findings.title: Lag lasted through most of the capture
key_findings.detail: 2 of 2 one-minute slices missed the target tick speed.
limitations: One-minute slices can hide shorter spikes inside that minute.

key_findings.title: A big chunk of time couldn’t be tied to a clear mod
key_findings.detail: About 23.7% of measured time was labeled unknown or native (JVM/native code or missing mod mapping).
limitations: Unknown/native can mean JVM code, physics natives, or missing class→mod mapping.
Don’t invent a mod name from a package prefix.

key_findings.title: The host machine was using a lot of swap
key_findings.detail: Swap used 14.07 GiB of 98.81 GiB. If the host is actively swapping to disk, the whole machine can hitch for hundreds of ms.
limitations: Other programs on the host can own that swap too.
One snapshot cannot prove swap was thrashing during the worst tick.

key_findings.title: Garbage collection was active
key_findings.detail: About 118 GC collections were reported in the capture metadata.
limitations: Collection count is not pause length — check average pause time if lag feels hitchy.

key_findings.title: View or simulation distance is set high
key_findings.detail: These settings can add load. Try lowering one of them for a test — not a proven cause by itself.
limitations: Distance alone does not prove chunk loading was the lag.

key_findings.title: AFK players are never kicked for idle
key_findings.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 lets AFK players keep areas loaded forever.
limitations: That’s an ops choice — farm fail-safes matter more than the timeout alone.

key_findings.title: Full entity tracking range with high view distance
key_findings.detail: entity-broadcast-range-percentage=100 with view-distance=20 can make dense entity areas cost more to track for players.
limitations: Tracking cost is a secondary clue — not primary proof of tick lag.

key_findings.title: Neighbor-update chain limit is very high
key_findings.detail: max-chained-neighbor-updates=1000000 can let cascading redstone or machines hitch for longer.
limitations: This is a spike-risk setting — not proof of the worst tick in this capture.

key_findings.title: Spectators can generate new chunks
key_findings.detail: spectatorsGenerateChunks is on — flying in spectator can generate terrain and add load.
limitations: This is an occasional spike risk — not enough alone to explain long low TPS.

recommendations.title: Inspect Nether chunk 170, -88 first
recommendations.detail: the_nether chunk 170,-88 has 455 entities (mostly minecraft:experience_orb). Visit that spot in-game before changing global limits.
actions: Go near blocks ~2720, ~-1408 in Nether
Note what is producing the XP orbs (farm, hopper line, machine, leftover pile)
Fix or pause that one setup, then profile again with a similar player count
limitations: Clearing entities without fixing what makes them will not prove a lasting fix.
reversible_actions: Go near blocks ~2720, ~-1408 in Nether
Note what is producing the XP orbs (farm, hopper line, machine, leftover pile)
Fix or pause that one setup, then profile again with a similar player count
recommendations.why: This capture’s busiest chunk is a concrete place to look — clearer than guessing from mod percentages alone.

recommendations.title: Check Create farms and item piles before tweaking Create configs
recommendations.detail: Create shows up in stacks (~17.0% own, ~76% involvement) and the world is heavy on XP/items/glue. Start with the busy chunks and the machines feeding them — a Create config tweak won’t clear a flooded farm.
actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
limitations: A smaller percentage after a change does not prove what fixed the lag.
reversible_actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
recommendations.why: Create time plus a crowded automation/item composition usually means an in-world setup, not a random version bump.

recommendations.title: Check free RAM and whether the machine is swapping
recommendations.detail: Host swap was about 14.1 GiB during this capture. Confirm free memory and active swap before raising Minecraft’s max heap.
actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
limitations: Don’t assume Minecraft alone filled the host’s swap.
reversible_actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
recommendations.why: Swap pressure can hitch the whole machine even when Spark points at mods or entities.

recommendations.title: Lower view-distance from 20 for a short test
recommendations.detail: This capture used view-distance=20 while ticks looked slow. Try 18 temporarily — that cuts how far chunks stay loaded for players without touching simulation yet.
actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
limitations: If the two captures had different player activity, the comparison can be misleading.
reversible_actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
recommendations.why: View distance is high in the captured server.properties, so the advice names that setting instead of a generic tweak.

evidence_summary.what_happened: Your server was lagging — start with the findings below
evidence_summary.why_watchtower_says_this: About 19.3 TPS; typical tick ~51 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~62 ms; worst tick ~386 ms (1 min); worst recent hitch ~5.0 s (5 min).
evidence_summary.what_this_cannot_prove: A profile shows what was busy during the capture. It doesn’t prove the single cause or how much faster the server will get.

settings_advice.title: View distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 62ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 14% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested view-distance=5 (band 6–10).

settings_advice.title: Network compression
settings_advice.detail: Compression threshold 256 is in a common range.

settings_advice.title: Spawn protection
settings_advice.detail: Spawn protection 0 is an ops choice — not a primary lag lever.

settings_advice.title: Simulation distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 62ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 14% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested simulation-distance=3 (band 4–8). Keep sim ≤ view.

settings_advice.title: Entity broadcast range
settings_advice.detail: With high view-distance/CPU pressure, consider lowering entity broadcast toward 50%.

settings_advice.title: Rate limit
settings_advice.detail: Packet rate-limit 0 — leave alone unless you are mitigating connection abuse.

settings_advice.title: Max tick time
settings_advice.detail: Watchdog headroom looks fine for modded dedicated servers.

settings_advice.title: Player idle timeout
settings_advice.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 never kicks AFK players — they can keep chunks loaded. Consider 30–60 minutes.

settings_advice.title: Sync chunk writes
settings_advice.detail: sync-chunk-writes=true can stutter the tick loop on dedicated hosts — consider false (Paper already forces this).

settings_advice.title: Max chained neighbor updates
settings_advice.detail: Neighbor-update chain limit 1000000 is very high — consider 100000 to limit redstone/hopper storms.

settings_advice.title: Region file compression
settings_advice.detail: deflate is the common default; lz4 is fine on modern JVMs.

settings_advice.title: Native transport
settings_advice.detail: Native transport enabled — fine on Linux.

verdict.summary: TPS 17.7 · typical tick 56 ms · slow ticks (p95) 71 ms · worst hitch 5.4 s · 7 players · 1283 entities

key_findings.title: CPU time profile
key_findings.detail: Percentages show how often Spark saw each piece of code on the main Server thread during the capture — not every millisecond of the whole machine.
limitations: A profile only covers the time window that was recorded.

key_findings.title: Your server was running slow
key_findings.detail: About 17.7 TPS; typical tick ~56 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~71 ms; worst tick ~426 ms (1 min); worst recent hitch ~5.4 s (5 min).
limitations: These numbers describe the capture window. They do not name a single cause.

key_findings.title: neruina shows up often in the stack, but rarely as the heavy step
key_findings.detail: Spark saw neruina on about 45% of samples, but only about 0.0% as the code doing the work at that moment.
limitations: It may be on the path without being the heavy part.
Don’t treat this as proof this mod alone made the server lag.

key_findings.title: More Create glue-style entities than usual
key_findings.detail: Of 1283 loaded entities: about 17% XP+items, 15% glue-style entities (e.g. Create glue), 33% XP+items+glue combined.
limitations: These are counts of what is loaded — not proof they made the server lag.
Worth checking in-world first — common lag suspects, not a proven tick cost.

key_findings.title: create used a large share of server time
key_findings.detail: About 12.6% of measured Server-thread time was spent inside create itself (hot step: KineticBlockEntity.handler$bal000$create_tweaked_controllers$getFlickerScoreMixin).
limitations: This shows where time showed up in the sample — not proof this mod alone made the server lag.
Sampling can miss short bursts or mis-label some code.

key_findings.title: Players online during the capture
key_findings.detail: 7 players were online when these stats were collected.
limitations: Player count alone does not say where they were or what they were doing.

key_findings.title: Lag lasted through most of the capture
key_findings.detail: 2 of 2 one-minute slices missed the target tick speed.
limitations: One-minute slices can hide shorter spikes inside that minute.

key_findings.title: A big chunk of time couldn’t be tied to a clear mod
key_findings.detail: About 28.4% of measured time was labeled unknown or native (JVM/native code or missing mod mapping).
limitations: Unknown/native can mean JVM code, physics natives, or missing class→mod mapping.
Don’t invent a mod name from a package prefix.

key_findings.title: The host machine was using a lot of swap
key_findings.detail: Swap used 14.70 GiB of 98.81 GiB. If the host is actively swapping to disk, the whole machine can hitch for hundreds of ms.
limitations: Other programs on the host can own that swap too.
One snapshot cannot prove swap was thrashing during the worst tick.

key_findings.title: Garbage collection was active
key_findings.detail: About 11441 GC collections were reported in the capture metadata.
limitations: Collection count is not pause length — check average pause time if lag feels hitchy.

key_findings.title: View or simulation distance is set high
key_findings.detail: These settings can add load. Try lowering one of them for a test — not a proven cause by itself.
limitations: Distance alone does not prove chunk loading was the lag.

key_findings.title: AFK players are never kicked for idle
key_findings.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 lets AFK players keep areas loaded forever.
limitations: That’s an ops choice — farm fail-safes matter more than the timeout alone.

key_findings.title: Full entity tracking range with high view distance
key_findings.detail: entity-broadcast-range-percentage=100 with view-distance=20 can make dense entity areas cost more to track for players.
limitations: Tracking cost is a secondary clue — not primary proof of tick lag.

key_findings.title: Neighbor-update chain limit is very high
key_findings.detail: max-chained-neighbor-updates=1000000 can let cascading redstone or machines hitch for longer.
limitations: This is a spike-risk setting — not proof of the worst tick in this capture.

key_findings.title: Spectators can generate new chunks
key_findings.detail: spectatorsGenerateChunks is on — flying in spectator can generate terrain and add load.
limitations: This is an occasional spike risk — not enough alone to explain long low TPS.

recommendations.title: Check Create farms and item piles before tweaking Create configs
recommendations.detail: Create shows up in stacks (~12.6% own, ~64% involvement) and the world is heavy on XP/items/glue. Start with the busy chunks and the machines feeding them — a Create config tweak won’t clear a flooded farm.
actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
limitations: A smaller percentage after a change does not prove what fixed the lag.
reversible_actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
recommendations.why: Create time plus a crowded automation/item composition usually means an in-world setup, not a random version bump.

recommendations.title: Check free RAM and whether the machine is swapping
recommendations.detail: Host swap was about 14.7 GiB during this capture. Confirm free memory and active swap before raising Minecraft’s max heap.
actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
limitations: Don’t assume Minecraft alone filled the host’s swap.
reversible_actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
recommendations.why: Swap pressure can hitch the whole machine even when Spark points at mods or entities.

recommendations.title: Lower view-distance from 20 for a short test
recommendations.detail: This capture used view-distance=20 while ticks looked slow. Try 18 temporarily — that cuts how far chunks stay loaded for players without touching simulation yet.
actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
limitations: If the two captures had different player activity, the comparison can be misleading.
reversible_actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
recommendations.why: View distance is high in the captured server.properties, so the advice names that setting instead of a generic tweak.

settings_advice.title: View distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 71ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 15% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested view-distance=5 (band 6–10).

settings_advice.title: Network compression
settings_advice.detail: Compression threshold 256 is in a common range.

settings_advice.title: Spawn protection
settings_advice.detail: Spawn protection 0 is an ops choice — not a primary lag lever.

settings_advice.title: Simulation distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 71ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 15% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested simulation-distance=3 (band 4–8). Keep sim ≤ view.

settings_advice.title: Entity broadcast range
settings_advice.detail: With high view-distance/CPU pressure, consider lowering entity broadcast toward 50%.

settings_advice.title: Rate limit
settings_advice.detail: Packet rate-limit 0 — leave alone unless you are mitigating connection abuse.

settings_advice.title: Max tick time
settings_advice.detail: Watchdog headroom looks fine for modded dedicated servers.

settings_advice.title: Player idle timeout
settings_advice.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 never kicks AFK players — they can keep chunks loaded. Consider 30–60 minutes.

settings_advice.title: Sync chunk writes
settings_advice.detail: sync-chunk-writes=true can stutter the tick loop on dedicated hosts — consider false (Paper already forces this).

settings_advice.title: Max chained neighbor updates
settings_advice.detail: Neighbor-update chain limit 1000000 is very high — consider 100000 to limit redstone/hopper storms.

settings_advice.title: Region file compression
settings_advice.detail: deflate is the common default; lz4 is fine on modern JVMs.

settings_advice.title: Native transport
settings_advice.detail: Native transport enabled — fine on Linux.

verdict.headline: Your server was lagging — start with the findings below
verdict.summary: TPS 17.5 · typical tick 55 ms · slow ticks (p95) 68 ms · worst recent tick 894 ms · 8 players · 2281 entities

key_findings.title: CPU time profile
key_findings.detail: Percentages show how often Spark saw each piece of code on the main Server thread during the capture — not every millisecond of the whole machine.
limitations: A profile only covers the time window that was recorded.

key_findings.title: Your server was lagging
key_findings.detail: About 17.5 TPS; typical tick ~55 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~68 ms; worst tick ~102 ms (1 min); worst recent tick ~894 ms (5 min).
limitations: These numbers describe the capture window. They do not name a single cause.

key_findings.title: More Create glue-style entities than usual
key_findings.detail: Of 2281 loaded entities: about 23% XP+items, 19% glue-style entities (e.g. Create glue), 43% XP+items+glue combined.
limitations: These are counts of what is loaded — not proof they made the server lag.
Worth checking in-world first — common lag suspects, not a proven tick cost.

key_findings.title: create used a large share of server time
key_findings.detail: About 10.2% of measured Server-thread time was spent inside create itself (hot step: AbstractContraptionEntity.tickActors).
limitations: This shows where time showed up in the sample — not proof this mod alone made the server lag.
Sampling can miss short bursts or mis-label some code.

key_findings.title: Players online during the capture
key_findings.detail: 8 players were online when these stats were collected.
limitations: Player count alone does not say where they were or what they were doing.

key_findings.title: Lag lasted through most of the capture
key_findings.detail: 2 of 2 one-minute slices missed the target tick speed.
limitations: One-minute slices can hide shorter spikes inside that minute.

key_findings.title: A big chunk of time couldn’t be tied to a clear mod
key_findings.detail: About 25.8% of measured time was labeled unknown or native (JVM/native code or missing mod mapping).
limitations: Unknown/native can mean JVM code, physics natives, or missing class→mod mapping.
Don’t invent a mod name from a package prefix.

key_findings.title: The host machine was using a lot of swap
key_findings.detail: Swap used 14.10 GiB of 98.81 GiB. If the host is actively swapping to disk, the whole machine can hitch for hundreds of ms.
limitations: Other programs on the host can own that swap too.
One snapshot cannot prove swap was thrashing during the worst tick.

key_findings.title: Garbage collection was active
key_findings.detail: About 581 GC collections were reported in the capture metadata.
limitations: Collection count is not pause length — check average pause time if lag feels hitchy.

key_findings.title: AFK players are never kicked for idle
key_findings.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 lets AFK players keep areas loaded forever.
limitations: That’s an ops choice — farm fail-safes matter more than the timeout alone.

key_findings.title: Neighbor-update chain limit is very high
key_findings.detail: max-chained-neighbor-updates=1000000 can let cascading redstone or machines hitch for longer.
limitations: This is a spike-risk setting — not proof of the worst tick in this capture.

key_findings.title: Spectators can generate new chunks
key_findings.detail: spectatorsGenerateChunks is on — flying in spectator can generate terrain and add load.
limitations: This is an occasional spike risk — not enough alone to explain long low TPS.

recommendations.title: Check Create farms and item piles before tweaking Create configs
recommendations.detail: Create shows up in stacks (~10.2% own, ~46% involvement) and the world is heavy on XP/items/glue. Start with the busy chunks and the machines feeding them — a Create config tweak won’t clear a flooded farm.
actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
limitations: A smaller percentage after a change does not prove what fixed the lag.
reversible_actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
recommendations.why: Create time plus a crowded automation/item composition usually means an in-world setup, not a random version bump.

recommendations.title: Check free RAM and whether the machine is swapping
recommendations.detail: Host swap was about 14.1 GiB during this capture. Confirm free memory and active swap before raising Minecraft’s max heap.
actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
limitations: Don’t assume Minecraft alone filled the host’s swap.
reversible_actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
recommendations.why: Swap pressure can hitch the whole machine even when Spark points at mods or entities.

recommendations.title: Lower max-chained-neighbor-updates from 1000000 for a spike test
recommendations.detail: Create is present and max-chained-neighbor-updates is very high. That can let cascading redstone/machine updates hitch longer — useful as a spike test after world hotspots are checked.
actions: Back up server.properties
Try max-chained-neighbor-updates=100000 for a short test
Profile during a known redstone/Create hitch, then restore if needed
limitations: If the two captures had different player activity, the comparison can be misleading.
reversible_actions: Back up server.properties
Try max-chained-neighbor-updates=100000 for a short test
Profile during a known redstone/Create hitch, then restore if needed
recommendations.why: High neighbor-update chains pair poorly with automation-heavy packs.

evidence_summary.why_watchtower_says_this: About 17.5 TPS; typical tick ~55 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~68 ms; worst tick ~102 ms (1 min); worst recent tick ~894 ms (5 min).

settings_advice.title: View distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 68ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 14% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested view-distance=5 (band 6–10).

settings_advice.title: Network compression
settings_advice.detail: Compression threshold 256 is in a common range.

settings_advice.title: Spawn protection
settings_advice.detail: Spawn protection 0 is an ops choice — not a primary lag lever.

settings_advice.title: Simulation distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 68ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 14% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested simulation-distance=3 (band 4–8). Keep sim ≤ view.

settings_advice.title: Entity broadcast range
settings_advice.detail: With high view-distance/CPU pressure, consider lowering entity broadcast toward 75%.

settings_advice.title: Rate limit
settings_advice.detail: Packet rate-limit 0 — leave alone unless you are mitigating connection abuse.

settings_advice.title: Max tick time
settings_advice.detail: Watchdog headroom looks fine for modded dedicated servers.

settings_advice.title: Player idle timeout
settings_advice.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 never kicks AFK players — they can keep chunks loaded. Consider 30–60 minutes.

settings_advice.title: Sync chunk writes
settings_advice.detail: sync-chunk-writes=true can stutter the tick loop on dedicated hosts — consider false (Paper already forces this).

settings_advice.title: Max chained neighbor updates
settings_advice.detail: Neighbor-update chain limit 1000000 is very high — consider 100000 to limit redstone/hopper storms.

settings_advice.title: Region file compression
settings_advice.detail: deflate is the common default; lz4 is fine on modern JVMs.

settings_advice.title: Native transport
settings_advice.detail: Native transport enabled — fine on Linux.

verdict.headline: Your server was lagging — start with the findings below
verdict.summary: TPS 7.7 · typical tick 117 ms · slow ticks (p95) 144 ms · worst hitch 4.2 s · 7 players · 2121 entities

key_findings.title: CPU time profile
key_findings.detail: Percentages show how often Spark saw each piece of code on the main Server thread during the capture — not every millisecond of the whole machine.
limitations: A profile only covers the time window that was recorded.

key_findings.title: Your server was running slow
key_findings.detail: About 7.7 TPS (about half speed); typical tick ~117 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~144 ms; worst tick ~469 ms (1 min); worst recent hitch ~4.2 s (5 min).
limitations: These numbers describe the capture window. They do not name a single cause.

key_findings.title: sable shows up often in the stack, but rarely as the heavy step
key_findings.detail: Spark saw sable on about 100% of samples, but only about 3.0% as the code doing the work at that moment.
limitations: It may be on the path without being the heavy part.
Don’t treat this as proof this mod alone made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Lots of XP, dropped items, or glue entities
key_findings.detail: Of 2121 loaded entities: about 50% XP+items, 6% glue-style entities (e.g. Create glue), 56% XP+items+glue combined; top custom is honey_glue (~5%).
limitations: These are counts of what is loaded — not proof they made the server lag.
Worth checking in-world first — common lag suspects, not a proven tick cost.

key_findings.title: Most entities are packed into a few chunks
key_findings.detail: The top 20 busy chunks hold 45% of loaded entities (across 620 chunks that have any).
limitations: This helps you know where to look — it does not prove those chunks made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Crowded chunk found
key_findings.detail: the_nether chunk 170,-78 has 342 entities (mostly minecraft:experience_orb).
limitations: A crowded chunk is a clue to check in-world — not proof it made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Busy chunks with nobody in that world
key_findings.detail: 2 busy chunks were in worlds with no located players (the_nether).
limitations: No one online there can mean chunk loaders or leftover loaded farms — not proven from this profile alone.
The profile has no chunk-ticket list, so force-loading is not proven.

key_findings.title: Create showed up in the sample stacks
key_findings.detail: Create accounted for about 7.8% of measured Server-thread time — visible in stacks, below the usual “large share” bar.
limitations: Presence is not proof Create caused lag; check World composition and call stacks if machines look busy.

key_findings.title: Players online during the capture
key_findings.detail: 7 players were online when these stats were collected.
limitations: Player count alone does not say where they were or what they were doing.

key_findings.title: Lag lasted through most of the capture
key_findings.detail: 2 of 2 one-minute slices missed the target tick speed.
limitations: One-minute slices can hide shorter spikes inside that minute.

key_findings.title: A big chunk of time couldn’t be tied to a clear mod
key_findings.detail: About 45.6% of measured time was labeled unknown or native (JVM/native code or missing mod mapping).
limitations: Unknown/native can mean JVM code, physics natives, or missing class→mod mapping.
Don’t invent a mod name from a package prefix.

key_findings.title: Lag with only moderate CPU use
key_findings.detail: Process CPU was about 21% while ticks looked bad. Minecraft’s tick mostly runs on one thread, so low total CPU does not mean that thread had spare room.
limitations: Moderate total CPU does not mean the tick thread was free.
This pattern does not name which mod or farm is responsible.

key_findings.title: The host machine was using a lot of swap
key_findings.detail: Swap used 14.21 GiB of 98.81 GiB. If the host is actively swapping to disk, the whole machine can hitch for hundreds of ms.
limitations: Other programs on the host can own that swap too.
One snapshot cannot prove swap was thrashing during the worst tick.

key_findings.title: Garbage collection was active
key_findings.detail: About 9145 GC collections were reported in the capture metadata.
limitations: Collection count is not pause length — check average pause time if lag feels hitchy.

key_findings.title: View or simulation distance is set high
key_findings.detail: These settings can add load. Try lowering one of them for a test — not a proven cause by itself.
limitations: Distance alone does not prove chunk loading was the lag.

key_findings.title: AFK players are never kicked for idle
key_findings.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 lets AFK players keep areas loaded forever.
limitations: That’s an ops choice — farm fail-safes matter more than the timeout alone.

key_findings.title: Full entity tracking range with high view distance
key_findings.detail: entity-broadcast-range-percentage=100 with view-distance=20 can make dense entity areas cost more to track for players.
limitations: Tracking cost is a secondary clue — not primary proof of tick lag.

key_findings.title: Neighbor-update chain limit is very high
key_findings.detail: max-chained-neighbor-updates=1000000 can let cascading redstone or machines hitch for longer.
limitations: This is a spike-risk setting — not proof of the worst tick in this capture.

key_findings.title: Spectators can generate new chunks
key_findings.detail: spectatorsGenerateChunks is on — flying in spectator can generate terrain and add load.
limitations: This is an occasional spike risk — not enough alone to explain long low TPS.

recommendations.title: Inspect Nether chunk 170, -78 first
recommendations.detail: the_nether chunk 170,-78 has 342 entities (mostly minecraft:experience_orb). Visit that spot in-game before changing global limits.
actions: Go near blocks ~2720, ~-1248 in Nether
Note what is producing the XP orbs (farm, hopper line, machine, leftover pile)
Fix or pause that one setup, then profile again with a similar player count
limitations: Clearing entities without fixing what makes them will not prove a lasting fix.
reversible_actions: Go near blocks ~2720, ~-1248 in Nether
Note what is producing the XP orbs (farm, hopper line, machine, leftover pile)
Fix or pause that one setup, then profile again with a similar player count
recommendations.why: This capture’s busiest chunk is a concrete place to look — clearer than guessing from mod percentages alone.

recommendations.title: Check Create farms and item piles before tweaking Create configs
recommendations.detail: Create shows up in stacks (~7.8% own, ~38% involvement) and the world is heavy on XP/items/glue. Start with the busy chunks and the machines feeding them — a Create config tweak won’t clear a flooded farm.
actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
limitations: A smaller percentage after a change does not prove what fixed the lag.
reversible_actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping XP/items/glue
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
recommendations.why: Create time plus a crowded automation/item composition usually means an in-world setup, not a random version bump.

recommendations.title: Check free RAM and whether the machine is swapping
recommendations.detail: Host swap was about 14.2 GiB during this capture. Confirm free memory and active swap before raising Minecraft’s max heap.
actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
limitations: Don’t assume Minecraft alone filled the host’s swap.
reversible_actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
recommendations.why: Swap pressure can hitch the whole machine even when Spark points at mods or entities.

recommendations.title: Lower view-distance from 20 for a short test
recommendations.detail: This capture used view-distance=20 while ticks looked slow. Try 18 temporarily — that cuts how far chunks stay loaded for players without touching simulation yet.
actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
limitations: If the two captures had different player activity, the comparison can be misleading.
reversible_actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
recommendations.why: View distance is high in the captured server.properties, so the advice names that setting instead of a generic tweak.

evidence_summary.what_happened: Your server was lagging — start with the findings below
evidence_summary.why_watchtower_says_this: About 7.7 TPS (about half speed); typical tick ~117 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~144 ms; worst tick ~469 ms (1 min); worst recent hitch ~4.2 s (5 min).
evidence_summary.what_this_cannot_prove: A profile shows what was busy during the capture. It doesn’t prove the single cause or how much faster the server will get.

settings_advice.title: View distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 144ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 14% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested view-distance=5 (band 6–10).

settings_advice.title: Network compression
settings_advice.detail: Compression threshold 256 is in a common range.

settings_advice.title: Spawn protection
settings_advice.detail: Spawn protection 0 is an ops choice — not a primary lag lever.

settings_advice.title: Simulation distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 144ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 14% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested simulation-distance=3 (band 4–8). Keep sim ≤ view.

settings_advice.title: Entity broadcast range
settings_advice.detail: With high view-distance/CPU pressure, consider lowering entity broadcast toward 50%.

settings_advice.title: Rate limit
settings_advice.detail: Packet rate-limit 0 — leave alone unless you are mitigating connection abuse.

settings_advice.title: Max tick time
settings_advice.detail: Watchdog headroom looks fine for modded dedicated servers.

settings_advice.title: Player idle timeout
settings_advice.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 never kicks AFK players — they can keep chunks loaded. Consider 30–60 minutes.

settings_advice.title: Sync chunk writes
settings_advice.detail: sync-chunk-writes=true can stutter the tick loop on dedicated hosts — consider false (Paper already forces this).

settings_advice.title: Max chained neighbor updates
settings_advice.detail: Neighbor-update chain limit 1000000 is very high — consider 100000 to limit redstone/hopper storms.

settings_advice.title: Region file compression
settings_advice.detail: deflate is the common default; lz4 is fine on modern JVMs.

settings_advice.title: Native transport
settings_advice.detail: Native transport enabled — fine on Linux.

verdict.headline: Your server was lagging — start with the findings below
verdict.summary: TPS 12.0 · typical tick 82 ms · slow ticks (p95) 123 ms · worst recent tick 778 ms · 5 players · 2951 entities

key_findings.title: CPU time profile
key_findings.detail: Percentages show how often Spark saw each piece of code on the main Server thread during the capture — not every millisecond of the whole machine.
limitations: A profile only covers the time window that was recorded.

key_findings.title: Your server was running slow
key_findings.detail: About 12.0 TPS (about half speed); typical tick ~82 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~123 ms; worst tick ~592 ms (1 min); worst recent tick ~778 ms (5 min).
limitations: These numbers describe the capture window. They do not name a single cause.

key_findings.title: neruina shows up often in the stack, but rarely as the heavy step
key_findings.detail: Spark saw neruina on about 41% of samples, but only about 0.0% as the code doing the work at that moment.
limitations: It may be on the path without being the heavy part.
Don’t treat this as proof this mod alone made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Lots of XP, dropped items, or glue entities
key_findings.detail: Of 2951 loaded entities: about 47% XP+items, 4% glue-style entities (e.g. Create glue), 51% XP+items+glue combined; top custom is hanging_wire (~6%).
limitations: These are counts of what is loaded — not proof they made the server lag.
Worth checking in-world first — common lag suspects, not a proven tick cost.

key_findings.title: Crowded chunk found
key_findings.detail: overworld chunk -32,-22 has 208 entities (mostly minecraft:item).
limitations: A crowded chunk is a clue to check in-world — not proof it made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Busy chunks were far from online players
key_findings.detail: 5 busy chunks were at least 28 chunks away from the nearest player in that world (farthest 58).
limitations: This can mean chunk loaders or leftover loaded areas — the profile cannot prove which.
The profile has no chunk-ticket list, so force-loading is not proven.

key_findings.title: create used a large share of server time
key_findings.detail: About 8.2% of measured Server-thread time was spent inside create itself (hot step: ContinuousOBBCollider.collideMany).
limitations: This shows where time showed up in the sample — not proof this mod alone made the server lag.
Sampling can miss short bursts or mis-label some code.

key_findings.title: Players online during the capture
key_findings.detail: 5 players were online when these stats were collected.
limitations: Player count alone does not say where they were or what they were doing.

key_findings.title: Lag lasted through most of the capture
key_findings.detail: 10 of 10 one-minute slices missed the target tick speed.
limitations: One-minute slices can hide shorter spikes inside that minute.

key_findings.title: A big chunk of time couldn’t be tied to a clear mod
key_findings.detail: About 28.9% of measured time was labeled unknown or native (JVM/native code or missing mod mapping).
limitations: Unknown/native can mean JVM code, physics natives, or missing class→mod mapping.
Don’t invent a mod name from a package prefix.

key_findings.title: Lag with only moderate CPU use
key_findings.detail: Process CPU was about 15% while ticks looked bad. Minecraft’s tick mostly runs on one thread, so low total CPU does not mean that thread had spare room.
limitations: Moderate total CPU does not mean the tick thread was free.
This pattern does not name which mod or farm is responsible.

key_findings.title: The host machine was using a lot of swap
key_findings.detail: Swap used 10.63 GiB of 98.81 GiB. If the host is actively swapping to disk, the whole machine can hitch for hundreds of ms.
limitations: Other programs on the host can own that swap too.
One snapshot cannot prove swap was thrashing during the worst tick.

key_findings.title: Garbage collection was active
key_findings.detail: About 1482 GC collections were reported in the capture metadata.
limitations: Collection count is not pause length — check average pause time if lag feels hitchy.

key_findings.title: View or simulation distance is set high
key_findings.detail: These settings can add load. Try lowering one of them for a test — not a proven cause by itself.
limitations: Distance alone does not prove chunk loading was the lag.

key_findings.title: AFK players are never kicked for idle
key_findings.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 lets AFK players keep areas loaded forever.
limitations: That’s an ops choice — farm fail-safes matter more than the timeout alone.

key_findings.title: Full entity tracking range with high view distance
key_findings.detail: entity-broadcast-range-percentage=100 with view-distance=20 can make dense entity areas cost more to track for players.
limitations: Tracking cost is a secondary clue — not primary proof of tick lag.

key_findings.title: Neighbor-update chain limit is very high
key_findings.detail: max-chained-neighbor-updates=1000000 can let cascading redstone or machines hitch for longer.
limitations: This is a spike-risk setting — not proof of the worst tick in this capture.

key_findings.title: Spectators can generate new chunks
key_findings.detail: spectatorsGenerateChunks is on — flying in spectator can generate terrain and add load.
limitations: This is an occasional spike risk — not enough alone to explain long low TPS.

recommendations.title: Inspect Overworld chunk -32, -22 first
recommendations.detail: overworld chunk -32,-22 has 208 entities (mostly minecraft:item). Visit that spot in-game before changing global limits.
actions: Go near blocks ~-512, ~-352 in Overworld
Note what is producing the dropped items (farm, hopper line, machine, leftover pile)
Fix or pause that one setup, then profile again with a similar player count
limitations: Clearing entities without fixing what makes them will not prove a lasting fix.
reversible_actions: Go near blocks ~-512, ~-352 in Overworld
Note what is producing the dropped items (farm, hopper line, machine, leftover pile)
Fix or pause that one setup, then profile again with a similar player count
recommendations.why: This capture’s busiest chunk is a concrete place to look — clearer than guessing from mod percentages alone.

recommendations.title: Check Create farms and item piles before tweaking Create configs
recommendations.detail: Create shows up in stacks (~8.2% own, ~50% involvement) and the world is heavy on XP/items/glue. Start with the busy chunks and the machines feeding them — a Create config tweak won’t clear a flooded farm.
actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping items
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
limitations: A smaller percentage after a change does not prove what fixed the lag.
reversible_actions: Open World view and visit the busiest chunk near Create machines
Pause or empty one farm/contraption that is dumping items
Profile again under the same player load before changing Create’s global settings
recommendations.why: Create time plus a crowded automation/item composition usually means an in-world setup, not a random version bump.

recommendations.title: Check free RAM and whether the machine is swapping
recommendations.detail: Host swap was about 10.6 GiB during this capture. Confirm free memory and active swap before raising Minecraft’s max heap.
actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
limitations: Don’t assume Minecraft alone filled the host’s swap.
reversible_actions: Check free RAM and whether swap is actively moving (host tools)
Find other memory-heavy programs before raising Xmx
Leave room for the OS and other services
recommendations.why: Swap pressure can hitch the whole machine even when Spark points at mods or entities.

recommendations.title: Lower view-distance from 20 for a short test
recommendations.detail: This capture used view-distance=20 while ticks looked slow. Try 18 temporarily — that cuts how far chunks stay loaded for players without touching simulation yet.
actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
limitations: If the two captures had different player activity, the comparison can be misleading.
reversible_actions: Back up server.properties
Set view-distance=18 and restart/reload as your host requires
Profile again under the same play, then restore 20 if you need the range back
recommendations.why: View distance is high in the captured server.properties, so the advice names that setting instead of a generic tweak.

evidence_summary.what_happened: Your server was lagging — start with the findings below
evidence_summary.why_watchtower_says_this: About 12.0 TPS (about half speed); typical tick ~82 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~123 ms; worst tick ~592 ms (1 min); worst recent tick ~778 ms (5 min).
evidence_summary.what_this_cannot_prove: A profile shows what was busy during the capture. It doesn’t prove the single cause or how much faster the server will get.

settings_advice.title: View distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 123ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 11% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested view-distance=6 (band 6–10).

settings_advice.title: Network compression
settings_advice.detail: Compression threshold 256 is in a common range.

settings_advice.title: Spawn protection
settings_advice.detail: Spawn protection 0 is an ops choice — not a primary lag lever.

settings_advice.title: Simulation distance
settings_advice.detail: MSPT p95 123ms — prefer lowering simulation-distance first. Swap 11% in use — cut distances more aggressively. Suggested simulation-distance=3 (band 4–8). Keep sim ≤ view.

settings_advice.title: Entity broadcast range
settings_advice.detail: With high view-distance/CPU pressure, consider lowering entity broadcast toward 50%.

settings_advice.title: Rate limit
settings_advice.detail: Packet rate-limit 0 — leave alone unless you are mitigating connection abuse.

settings_advice.title: Max tick time
settings_advice.detail: Watchdog headroom looks fine for modded dedicated servers.

settings_advice.title: Player idle timeout
settings_advice.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 never kicks AFK players — they can keep chunks loaded. Consider 30–60 minutes.

settings_advice.title: Sync chunk writes
settings_advice.detail: sync-chunk-writes=true can stutter the tick loop on dedicated hosts — consider false (Paper already forces this).

settings_advice.title: Max chained neighbor updates
settings_advice.detail: Neighbor-update chain limit 1000000 is very high — consider 100000 to limit redstone/hopper storms.

settings_advice.title: Region file compression
settings_advice.detail: deflate is the common default; lz4 is fine on modern JVMs.

settings_advice.title: Native transport
settings_advice.detail: Native transport enabled — fine on Linux.

verdict.summary: TPS 20.0 · typical tick 1 ms · slow ticks (p95) 2 ms · 0 players · 200 entities

key_findings.title: CPU time profile
key_findings.detail: Percentages show how often Spark saw each piece of code on the main Server thread during the capture — not every millisecond of the whole machine.
limitations: A profile only covers the time window that was recorded.

key_findings.title: Tick speed looked healthy during the capture
key_findings.detail: About 20.0 TPS; typical tick ~1 ms; slow ticks (p95) ~2 ms; worst tick ~5 ms (1 min); worst recent tick ~175 ms (5 min).
limitations: These numbers describe the capture window. They do not name a single cause.

key_findings.title: Many marker entities are loaded
key_findings.detail: Of 200 loaded entities: about 58% are minecraft:marker (115). Custom crowd leader: mushling.
limitations: These are counts of what is loaded — not proof they made the server lag.
Worth checking in-world first — common lag suspects, not a proven tick cost.

key_findings.title: Entities are packed into a few chunks (tick speed still looked fine)
key_findings.detail: The top 20 busy chunks hold 96% of loaded entities (across 29 chunks that have any). Tick speed looked healthy with nobody online — useful map context, not an urgent lag alarm.
limitations: This helps you know where to look — it does not prove those chunks made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Marker-heavy chunk (server still looked healthy)
key_findings.detail: overworld chunk -3,34 has 102 entities (mostly markers). Useful later if lag appears — not a primary next step while TPS looks fine with nobody online.
limitations: A crowded chunk is a clue to check in-world — not proof it made the server lag.

key_findings.title: Create showed up in the sample stacks
key_findings.detail: Create accounted for about 0.1% of measured Server-thread time — visible in stacks, below the usual “large share” bar.
limitations: Presence is not proof Create caused lag; check World composition and call stacks if machines look busy.

key_findings.title: Many datapacks were loaded
key_findings.detail: 25 datapacks appear in this capture (17 marked world/unknown source). Worldgen and custom packs can change what loads — not a proven tick cost by themselves.
limitations: Datapack names are metadata from Spark — disable or compare packs only with a before/after profile.

key_findings.title: Players online during the capture
key_findings.detail: 0 players were online when these stats were collected.
limitations: Player count alone does not say where they were or what they were doing.

key_findings.title: A big chunk of time couldn’t be tied to a clear mod
key_findings.detail: About 99.0% of measured time was labeled unknown or native (JVM/native code or missing mod mapping).
limitations: Unknown/native can mean JVM code, physics natives, or missing class→mod mapping.
Don’t invent a mod name from a package prefix.

key_findings.title: Garbage collection was active
key_findings.detail: About 87 GC collections were reported in the capture metadata.
limitations: Collection count is not pause length — check average pause time if lag feels hitchy.

key_findings.title: AFK players are never kicked for idle
key_findings.detail: player-idle-timeout=0 lets AFK players keep areas loaded forever.
limitations: That’s an ops choice — farm fail-safes matter more than the timeout alone.

key_findings.title: Neighbor-update chain limit is very high
key_findings.detail: max-chained-neighbor-updates=1000000 can let cascading redstone or machines hitch for longer.
limitations: This is a spike-risk setting — not proof of the worst tick in this capture.

recommendations.title: Profile again under the same kind of play
recommendations.detail: After one focused change, run another capture under the same kind of load to see if the same signals remain.
actions: /spark profiler start
Wait 30–60 seconds while the lag is happening
/spark profiler stop --save-to-file
limitations: Compare captures only when player activity and server setup are similar.
reversible_actions: /spark profiler start
Wait 30–60 seconds while the lag is happening
/spark profiler stop --save-to-file
recommendations.why: Useful as a follow-up after a concrete change — not the first move when the profile already points somewhere.
